sights.address: Washington Park community area, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
sights.w: Olmsted & Vaux's 372-acre South Side park, home of Lorado Taft's 'Fountain of Time' and the DuSable museum.

sights.address: Evanston lakefront, IL (per NPS NHL record)
sights.w: Château-style 1894 lakefront mansion of Nobel laureate and US Vice President Charles G. Dawes — a National Historic Landmark run by the Evanston History Center.

sights.address: Lower West Side (Pilsen), around 18th St, Chicago (per Wikipedia / City of Chicago landmark district)
sights.w: National Register district of 1870s–1910s Bohemian worker cottages, storefronts and churches — now the heart of Mexican Pilsen and its murals along 16th and 18th Streets.

sights.address: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: The 1928 Spanish Baroque 'Gold Dome' fieldhouse, a gold-leafed Chicago Landmark towering over Garfield Park — under a $9M restoration.

sights.n: Holy Cross Church (Back of the Yards)
sights.address: 1740 W 46th St, Chicago, IL
sights.w: National Register Lithuanian church (1915) whose twin towers rise over Back of the Yards, the old stockyards neighbourhood.

sights.n: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Marquette Park)
sights.address: 6812 S Washtenaw Ave, Chicago, IL 60629
sights.w: Mid-century Lithuanian Catholic church facing Marquette Park, designed in Lithuanian folk style — the spiritual centre of Chicago's Lithuanian community.

sights.address: W 47th St a few blocks east of S Ashland Ave, Back of the Yards, Chicago
sights.w: A 93,500 sq ft former meatpacking plant turned net-zero vertical farm and food-business incubator, home to Whiner Beer.

sights.address: 11111 S Forrestville Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: George Pullman's 1881 Queen Anne hotel at the heart of his company town — now restored within Pullman National Historical Park.

sights.address: 11211 S St Lawrence Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: Pullman's 1882 serpentine-greenstone church, designed by Solon S. Beman as part of the model town.

sights.address: 1650 N Halsted St, Chicago, IL
sights.w: The ensemble theatre founded in 1974 by Gary Sinise, Terry Kinney and Jeff Perry — Tony-winning home of Malkovich, Metcalf and 'August: Osage County'.

sights.n: Old Town School of Folk Music
sights.address: 4545 N Lincoln Ave, Chicago, IL 60625
sights.w: Folk-music school and concert hall (founded 1957) in a restored 1929 library building on Lincoln Square's main street.

sights.address: 2045 N Lincoln Park West (in Lincoln Park), Chicago, IL
sights.w: The last tomb left from the old City Cemetery under Lincoln Park — Ira Couch's 1858 mausoleum, too heavy to move.

sights.address: 2122 N Clark St, Chicago, IL
sights.w: The garage site of Capone-era Chicago's most notorious hit (1929) — the building is gone; a fenced lawn marks the spot.

sights.address: Division St between Western Ave and California Ave, Chicago, IL 60622
sights.w: Humboldt Park's Puerto Rican main street, bracketed by two 59-ft, 45-ton steel Puerto Rican flags arching over Division Street — a designated Chicago Landmark.

sights.address: Forest Ave, Oak Park, IL (per Wikipedia)
sights.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1902 Prairie-style house on Forest Avenue — low roman-brick walls and a raised main floor, a National Historic Landmark.
sights.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

sights.n: Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ
sights.address: 4021 S State St, Chicago, IL
sights.w: Bronzeville church where Mamie Till-Mobley held her son Emmett Till's open-casket funeral in 1955 — part of the Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley National Monument (2023).

sights.address: 4339 S Lake Park Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: Kenwood two-flat where Muddy Waters lived and rehearsed (1954–74) — a Chicago Landmark being restored as the MOJO Muddy Waters museum.

sights.address: 2700 S Halsted St area (former Stearns Quarry), Bridgeport, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
sights.w: A 1830s limestone quarry turned 27-acre park — a fishing pond in the pit, terraced wetlands and the city's best skyline hill.

sights.address: New City / Back of the Yards, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
sights.w: Olmsted Brothers & Burnham 'neighbourhood park' (1905) ringed by a lagoon, with a Burnham-designed fieldhouse — a landmark of the South Parks reform movement.

sights.address: Back of the Yards, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
sights.w: One of the first 1905 South Parks small parks, built to give stockyards families a fieldhouse, baths and playgrounds.

sights.address: South Fork of the South Branch, Chicago River (headwaters, per Wikipedia)
sights.w: The stockyards' notorious waste channel — Upton Sinclair's 'Bubbly Creek' still burps methane from century-old sediment, now ringed by new trails.

sights.address: Alsip, IL (per Wikipedia)
sights.w: Historic African American cemetery — resting place of Emmett Till, Dinah Washington and Willie Dixon.

sights.n: Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley House
sights.address: 6427 S St Lawrence Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: The West Woodlawn two-flat Emmett Till left in 1955 — a Chicago Landmark (2021) being restored as a museum and community space.

sights.n: R. W. Evans House (Frank Lloyd Wright)
sights.address: 9914 S Longwood Dr, Chicago, IL
sights.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1908 hilltop Prairie house on Beverly's Longwood Drive ridge.
sights.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

sights.address: 1600–1800 blocks of W 104th Pl (Griffin Place), Beverly, Chicago
sights.w: A street of Prairie School houses (1909–14), seven by Walter Burley Griffin — later the designer of Canberra — a Chicago Landmark district.

sights.address: South Deering, east shore of Lake Calumet, Chicago
sights.w: A former slag dump turned the Park District's largest natural site (~300 acres) — wetlands, birding and a bike park with pump tracks.

sights.address: 87th St & Western Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: A 257-acre forest preserve inside city limits on Beverly's ridge — trails, a sledding hill and the Major Taylor Trail.

sights.n: National A. Philip Randolph Pullman Porter Museum
sights.address: 10406 S Maryland Ave, Chicago, IL
sights.w: Museum of the Pullman porters and the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters — the birthplace of Black labor history, within Pullman National Historical Park.
